title: Shuja-ud-Din Administrative Phase in Bengal
subtitle: Bengal under Shujauddin Muhammad Khan, 1727–1739
summary: Shujauddin Muhammad Khan became Nawab of Bengal in 1727 after Murshid Quli Khan’s death and governed until 1739. He appointed relatives and officials to provincial posts and pursued accommodation with zamindars. In 1733 Bihar was added to the Bengal subah, whose administration was divided among central Bengal, Dhaka, Bihar and Orissa; deputy governors oversaw the outlying divisions, and Alivardi Khan was placed in charge of Bihar.
whyItMatters: Shujauddin’s administrative phase shows the Bengal nawabate governing a large Mughal province through appointments and regional deputy administrations. The addition of Bihar and division into four charges were specific institutional changes of his reign. Banglapedia describes the period as generally peaceful, though Badiuzzaman’s revolt in Birbhum was suppressed.

Shujauddin’s administrative phase shows the Bengal nawabate governing a large Mughal province through appointments and regional deputy administrations. The addition of Bihar and division into four charges were specific institutional changes of his reign. Banglapedia describes the period as generally peaceful, though Badiuzzaman’s revolt in Birbhum was suppressed.
